author_notes: Slot slot_238 targets realstoman/react-tailwindcss-portfolio, a stable React/Tailwind portfolio with real multi-route structure (home, projects archive, project detail, about, contact) and local project image assets (web-project, mobile-project, ui-project, developer.svg, profile.jpeg). The native lever is the portfolio's OWN project grid category filter: the repo already ships a ProjectsFilter over the six real projects, and this L4 task upgrades it into a responsive tabbed "Project focus" control with a live result count that is shared across every route the grid appears on. The design keeps the original cards, project images, search input, case-study detail, biography, contact form, header, footer, indigo accent, GeneralSans typography, and light/dark theme, and repairs the tab row's mobile overflow plus its cross-page continuity.
design_constraints: Use the existing React component structure, Tailwind utility style, GeneralSans font classes, indigo action color, primary/secondary/ternary light and dark tokens, rounded card radius, and current container spacing.

Repair the project-focus filter in place inside the projects grid components (src/components/projects/ProjectsGrid.jsx and its filter styles) rather than deleting it or replacing it with unrelated markup.

Keep the original hero illustration, project grid, project search input, project detail gallery, client facts, about biography/counters, contact details/form, header links, Hire Me control, footer, and theme switcher available.

Keep the filter grounded in current repo data: the six project cards and their real categories (Web Application, Mobile Application, UI/UX Design). Do not invent fake categories, remote assets, or hidden verifier-only strings.

The filter tab row must be readable and contained on desktop, tablet, mobile, and dark theme without horizontal overflow, and the project grid below must keep its normal multi-column rhythm without overlapping cards.

change_completion: The "Project focus" category filter (All work / Web App / Mobile / UI / UX tabs plus a live count readout) is present on both the home overview grid and the dedicated Projects page.
Clicking a focus tab filters the project cards to that category and updates the readout to the matching "Showing N of 6 · <focus>" string.
The filter is implemented as a reusable grid control shared across the routes that show the grid, not a one-off block on a single page.
design_consistency: The filter tab row follows the existing Tailwind/GeneralSans/indigo/light-dark visual language and sits inside the normal projects section rather than replacing the grid with a new layout.
The home overview and Projects page retain their original visual hierarchy while gaining the same focus control and result count.
Dark theme and mobile states keep the tabs, active-tab highlight, and readout legible and visually integrated.
responsive: On a phone viewport the filter tab row wraps and stays within the mobile width with no horizontal overflow on the Projects page.
The project grid keeps its 1/2/3-column responsive rhythm on mobile, tablet, and desktop without overlapping or clipped cards.
regression: Original navigation links, logo, theme switcher, Hire Me control, project search input, project cards, project detail gallery, about counters, contact form/details, and footer remain present and functional.
No horizontal overflow or contrast failure is introduced on any route or viewport, and the light/dark theme + mobile navigation continue to work.

metadata.design_goal: repair the mobile horizontal overflow of the shared portfolio proof continuity strip without disrupting proof content, DOM, or original page identities
metadata.source_repo_kind: React/Tailwind multi-route portfolio with local project imagery, project archive, project detail, about counters, contact form, light/dark theme, and responsive nav.

problem_statement: This React/Tailwind portfolio shows its work in a project grid that appears on both the home overview and the dedicated Projects page. The grid carries a native "Project focus" filter: a labelled row of category tabs (All work, Web App, Mobile, UI / UX) with a live result-count readout ("Showing N of 6 · <focus>"). Selecting a tab filters the six real project cards to that category and updates the readout. Two continuity defects remain. (1) Responsive: on a phone viewport the filter tab row is authored as a single fixed-width nowrap strip wider than the screen, so the Projects page overflows horizontally. (2) Cross-page: the filter rail was only mounted on the dedicated Projects page and is missing from the home overview grid, so the focus control does not travel with the grid across routes. Repair the filter so the tab row wraps and stays within the mobile viewport with no horizontal overflow, and so the "Project focus" rail is present on every route where the project grid is shown (home and Projects), while keeping the tab filtering and the live count readout correct and legible on desktop, tablet, mobile, and dark theme.
required_content: The "Project focus" filter tab row fits within the mobile viewport with no horizontal overflow on the Projects page (mobile document width within the responsive tolerance).

The four focus tabs (All work, Web App, Mobile, UI / UX) and the live "Showing N of 6 · <focus>" readout are present and legible on every route where the project grid appears, on desktop, tablet, mobile, and dark theme.
The "Project focus" rail appears on BOTH the home overview grid and the dedicated Projects page (cross-page continuity), not only on the Projects page.
Clicking a focus tab filters the six project cards to that category AND updates the count readout to the matching label (e.g. "Showing 2 of 6 · Web App").
Original navigation, logo, theme switcher, Hire Me control, project search input, project cards, project detail gallery, about counters, contact form, contact details, and footer remain present.
The repair is source-level React/Tailwind layout + wiring work on the grid filter, not generated build edits, screenshots, hidden-only text, or remote assets.
state_constraints: desktop_initial captures the original hero and the shared portfolio proof continuity strip laid out correctly on desktop.
desktop_projects captures the archive/filter route with the proof strip and original project search/category controls still available.
desktop_project_detail captures the case-study route with the proof strip, gallery, project metadata, and detail sections preserved.
desktop_about captures biography/counter/client continuity with the proof strip visible.
desktop_contact captures the proof strip plus original contact form and contact details.
desktop_dark_home verifies the proof strip is integrated with the existing dark theme.
tablet_projects verifies archive/proof layout containment on tablet.
mobile_initial verifies the proof continuity strip fits on the mobile home route without horizontal overflow.
mobile_nav_open verifies the original mobile menu still opens and the page still fits after the repair.
mobile_contact verifies the proof strip and contact content fit on mobile without horizontal overflow.
